user_goal: Make Plotkeeper reliably open the live dashboard for attached Codex tasks, prevent duplicate canonical runs, test and publish the repair with a changelog and release, then notify every currently attached Codex task to update and continue.

authority.verbatim_text: is it updated and tested good and clean across the board? If so, update the repo, add a changelog and release, and then let me know what current threads are utilizing it by sessionID and then send each one a specific "UPDATE PLOTKEEPER AND CONTINUE YOUR TURN" message (with instrucitons on how to do so

baseline.protection_evidence: Local main, origin/main, and public main are identical at the attested complete-bundle release.
baseline.selection_reason: Current public Plotkeeper release before the panel reliability correction.

resources: Installed Codex skills, hooks, and Plotkeeper plugin
GitHub EmergentKnowledgeGroup/PLOTKEEPER main, variables, secret names, Actions, tags, and Releases
Currently attached Codex tasks identified from the Plotkeeper ledger and Codex task registry
semantic_changes: Serve dashboard assets from a path valid in source and installed layouts and return explicit HTTP errors instead of empty sockets.
Make installation or startup replace a stale Plotkeeper process and prove the dashboard root, not only health.
Reuse one canonical active run per root Codex task and prevent message-event pseudo-roots from creating duplicate runs.
Make panel-open success contingent on a valid dashboard response.
Document, version, publish, and notify attached tasks with exact update-and-continue instructions.
Do not alter goal-contract, review, guard, release-verifier, attribution, license, or evidence-integrity semantics.
Do not close, delete, merge, or reassign existing Plotkeeper runs automatically.
Do not message tasks that cannot be reconciled to a currently existing Codex task.
Do not expose secrets, personal datasets, review receipts, calibration history, or unrelated project content.

invariants: The dashboard root returns valid HTML while health remains green in source, installed, and restarted-service execution paths.
A root Codex task maps to one canonical active Plotkeeper run; children attach without duplicate roots.
Panel-open claims are verified and fail closed.
Existing ledger history is preserved and no active task loses its contract or run identity.
The exact candidate passes independent review, public CI, and live post-release attestation before task notification.

acceptance_cases.promised_behavior: Opening Plotkeeper from an attached Codex task displays the current dashboard and its canonical run.
acceptance_cases.forbidden_behavior: A health-only success, empty HTTP response, stale process, missing asset, or unverified panel marker may be reported as opened.
acceptance_cases.target_and_actor: A Codex user opening the right-side Plotkeeper panel.

acceptance_cases.promised_behavior: Repeated events and child activity reuse the canonical active run for the root task.
acceptance_cases.forbidden_behavior: Message IDs, repeated activation, or worktree variants may create competing root runs for one task.
acceptance_cases.target_and_actor: Plotkeeper session scanner and ledger processing live Codex tasks.

acceptance_cases.promised_behavior: The repaired candidate is versioned, documented, independently reviewed, published, and communicated to every currently attached live Codex task.
acceptance_cases.forbidden_behavior: No stale candidate, failed CI, missing release note, unverifiable task, or generic message may be represented as complete.
acceptance_cases.target_and_actor: Repository users and current Plotkeeper-enabled Codex tasks.

proof_requirements.claim: HTTP dashboard handling is explicit and reliable.
proof_requirements.command_or_read_only_check: Exercise /health, /, static assets, missing assets, and handler exceptions.
proof_requirements.expected_observation: Valid responses with no empty socket.

proof_requirements.claim: Install/start replaces stale code and waits for the dashboard.
proof_requirements.required_environment: Fresh isolated install and live local service
proof_requirements.command_or_read_only_check: Install, restart, compare code/assets, and fetch dashboard HTML.
proof_requirements.expected_observation: The current candidate owns the listener and serves current HTML.

proof_requirements.claim: Panel success is tied to usable dashboard content.
proof_requirements.required_environment: Codex integration and panel dispatch contract
proof_requirements.command_or_read_only_check: Test success and failure paths and inspect the emitted marker.
proof_requirements.expected_observation: Success only follows verified dashboard availability.

proof_requirements.claim: Canonical run attachment is idempotent and history-preserving.
proof_requirements.required_environment: Synthetic scanner fixtures plus a read-only reconciliation of the live ledger
proof_requirements.command_or_read_only_check: Replay root, message, child, repeated, and worktree events.
proof_requirements.expected_observation: One canonical root run with children attached and no destructive ledger mutation.

proof_requirements.claim: The exact candidate is clean, reviewed, documented, released, and publicly green.
proof_requirements.required_environment: Git candidate, independent review, GitHub main/tag/release/Actions
proof_requirements.command_or_read_only_check: Run all tests, clean install/live verification, signed review chain, guarded push, release creation, and attestation.
proof_requirements.expected_observation: Exact public SHA and release tag pass all gates.

proof_requirements.claim: Every currently attached live Codex task receives specific update and continuation instructions.
proof_requirements.required_environment: Plotkeeper ledger and Codex task registry after release
proof_requirements.command_or_read_only_check: Reconcile session IDs to tasks, send one tailored message per task, and record delivery receipts.
proof_requirements.expected_observation: Every reconciled current task has one successful delivery; unreconciled historical rows are reported, not messaged.

release_requirements.required_receipt: Exact candidate, dashboard/install/run/panel tests, clean diff, changelog/version/tag plan, rollback, signed review chain, and target reconciliation.

stop_conditions: Install or restart risks killing an unrelated listener.
Any test, independent review, guard, CI, release, or live attestation fails.
A task cannot be reconciled safely for messaging.
Any forbidden, unrelated, secret, cache, history, or unexplained diff appears.
known_discrepancies: The live listener began before the productized dashboard move and serves health while closing dashboard requests without a response.
The live ledger contains multiple OPEN runs for the same project/root-task families, including message-ID pseudo-roots.

requirement_trace.user_requirement: update the repo, add a changelog and release, identify current threads by sessionID, and send each update instructions
